findings.title: Delay damages of 2% of total fees per day, uncapped, with no relief for AtliQ- or client-caused delay
findings.quote: If Vendor fails to achieve any Delivery Date, Vendor shall pay AtliQ, as liquidated damages, an amount equal to two percent (2%) of the Total Fees for each calendar day from the Delivery Date until the date the applicable Deliverable is accepted.
findings.explanation: Each day late costs 2% x INR 8,40,000 = INR 16,800, calculated on the whole contract rather than the late deliverable, with no cap; after 50 days the vendor would owe 100% of all fees, on top of actual damages (§11.3). The clock runs 'until the date the Deliverable is accepted', and AtliQ alone decides acceptance, with 15 days to test and no deemed acceptance (§3.1, §3.3), so the vendor pays while AtliQ is testing. There is no exclusion for delay caused by AtliQ or Rheinwerk, although the vendor works in 'AtliQ-provisioned cloud workspaces'; the same gap in the Brightwater contract led to a USD 18,400 delay claim against AtliQ. This fails 'LDs -> cap it. never open ended', sits far above the recorded 0.5% per week / 5% cap, and is the PixelCraft 1% per day penalty that Karandeep deleted for a 6-person agency. AtliQ itself would face only 0.5% per week, capped at 5%, from Rheinwerk (draft §8.2), so the flow-down is also mismatched.

The Supplier shall meet each Key Date. Time shall be of the essence in respect of the Key Dates.

findings.title: Payment up to 120 days after invoice, and only once Rheinwerk has paid AtliQ (pay-when-paid)
findings.quote: AtliQ's obligation to pay any invoice is conditional upon AtliQ's receipt of payment from the End Client for the corresponding services. AtliQ shall pay each properly submitted, undisputed invoice within fifteen (15) days after AtliQ receives the corresponding payment from the End Client, and in any event not later than one hundred and twenty (120) days after AtliQ's receipt of the invoice.
findings.explanation: The checklist says 30 days, 45 max; this is 120 days at the outer limit, which is 75 days beyond the maximum, and the obligation to pay does not even arise until Rheinwerk has paid AtliQ. The vendor invoices only monthly in arrears for accepted deliverables (§4.2), after up to 15 days of testing (§3.1), so the real wait is longer than 120 days from delivery. AtliQ is shifting its own client's payment risk onto a 12-person firm; this is the clause Kriti is pushing back on ('we're 12 people'). Karandeep's September note says a small agency should not get AtliQ's paper and feel the way he felt reading Brightwater's, and this is twice the 60 days PixelCraft objected to (cut to 30 days).

findings.title: Vendor's liability is unlimited while AtliQ's is capped at fees actually paid
findings.quote: NOTHING IN THIS AGREEMENT SHALL LIMIT OR EXCLUDE VENDOR'S LIABILITY FOR ANY LOSSES, WHETHER DIRECT OR INDIRECT, ARISING OUT OF OR RELATING TO THIS AGREEMENT, INCLUDING VENDOR'S INDEMNIFICATION OBLIGATIONS.
findings.explanation: A 12-person vendor on an INR 8,40,000 job would carry unlimited liability, including for indirect loss, while AtliQ's liability is limited to 'the fees actually paid' (§10.2) and AtliQ is excluded from indirect and consequential loss (§10.1). Because payment is conditional on Rheinwerk paying (§4.3), 'fees actually paid' can be nil. The checklist line is 'liability -> 1x fees. NOT unlimited', and Karandeep refused unlimited liability from Kessler on a EUR 120k deal; at PixelCraft he capped liability at fees for both sides. The cap is also not the same as AtliQ's own exposure to Rheinwerk, which is limited to total remuneration for ordinary negligence (Rheinwerk draft §9.2).

findings.title: Vendor indemnifies AtliQ even for AtliQ's own negligence
findings.quote: (a) the Services or Deliverables, (b) any breach of this Agreement by Vendor, (c) any claim by the End Client relating to the Services or Deliverables, or (d) any act or omission of Vendor Personnel, in each case regardless of whether such Losses are caused in whole or in part by the negligence of any AtliQ Indemnitee.
findings.explanation: Kriti would cover every loss connected with the services, including claims by Rheinwerk, even where AtliQ's own negligence caused them, and with no cap (§10.3). This is the opposite of 'indemnity -> mutual. we don't cover their mistakes'; the draft asks of a small vendor exactly what Karandeep refused from PayTrack ('we can't insure against PayTrack's own negligence'). The wording closely follows the Harrington draft's indemnity (§9.1), with the roles reversed.

findings.title: German plant and technician data goes to a vendor with no data-protection terms, its own platform, and no Rheinwerk consent on file
findings.quote: Source data comprises vibration, temperature and pressure sensor streams from End Client customer plants, together with maintenance work orders and technician logs (including technician names, shift identifiers and free-text notes). Vendor Personnel shall access data via AtliQ-provisioned cloud workspaces and Vendor's own labelling platform.
findings.explanation: The data includes technician names and free-text notes, so it contains personal data of Rheinwerk's side, and the vendor will also use its own labelling platform, so data leaves AtliQ's workspaces. The Kriti draft has no data-protection clause, no processing instructions and no security or breach terms; its confidentiality definition covers only information 'disclosed by or on behalf of AtliQ or the End Client'. Rheinwerk's draft allows subcontracting only with Rheinwerk's written consent (§15.3), requires its personnel to be AtliQ's own (§2.3) and requires a data processing agreement as Annex 3 (§13.1), which is not in the file. Kriti is scheduled to start 5 Oct, before the Rheinwerk contract is signed (needed by 15 Oct) and with no consent recorded.

findings.title: AtliQ can end on 7 days' notice without paying for work in progress; the vendor has no matching right
findings.quote: AtliQ may terminate this Agreement, in whole or in part, for any reason or no reason, upon seven (7) days' written notice to Vendor. Upon such termination, AtliQ's sole obligation shall be to pay Fees for Deliverables accepted by AtliQ prior to the effective date of termination; AtliQ shall have no obligation to pay for work in progress, unaccepted Deliverables, demobilization costs or anticipated profits.
findings.explanation: Only AtliQ can end for convenience, and the vendor must hand over incomplete work immediately (§5.4) with no payment for work in progress. The checklist line is 'termination -> they pay for work done', which is what AtliQ asks of its own clients (for example Trustline pays a pro rata share of any milestone in progress). Cure periods are 15 days for both sides (§5.2), so only the convenience right is lopsided. Exposure is bounded by the fee schedule, e.g. Batch 1 is INR 3,20,000 of the INR 8,40,000.

findings.title: Kriti keeps the annotation outputs and AtliQ gets only a non-transferable licence, while Rheinwerk's draft expects exclusive, transferable rights
findings.quote: Subject to payment of the applicable Fees, Vendor grants AtliQ a non-exclusive, non-transferable, perpetual licence to use the annotation outputs and Deliverables for the purposes of the End Client project, including delivery to the End Client.
findings.explanation: The definition of Deliverables (§1.2) includes labelled datasets and label files, but §7.2 says Kriti keeps 'annotation outputs' and §7.3 gives AtliQ only a licence for the End Client project. Rheinwerk's draft says that, apart from PipeKit, it acquires 'exclusive, perpetual, transferable and unrestricted' rights in all Work Results created specifically for it (§6.5). AtliQ cannot pass on rights it does not hold, so as drafted the two documents do not fit. Neither is signed, so this can be fixed before either is.

low.title: Several clauses are near-identical to the Harrington draft, with roles swapped
low.quote: Accordingly, if Contractor fails to achieve any Delivery Date, Contractor shall pay Client, as liquidated damages, an amount equal to two percent (2%) of the Total Contract Value for each calendar day from the Delivery Date until the date the applicable Deliverable is accepted.
low.note: The same 2% per day wording (here on the vendor), the 7-day no-pay termination for convenience (Harrington §5.3), the indemnity covering the other side's negligence (§9.1), the 'no deemed acceptance' and 'fees firm and fixed' clauses, and the one-way liability clause (§10.3) all come from the Harrington paper Jay used as the template. Harrington's own payment term is 90 days; this draft goes to 120 and adds pay-when-paid.

low.title: AtliQ may set off its delay damages against what it owes
low.quote: AtliQ may set off against any amount owed to Vendor any amount owed by Vendor to AtliQ under this Agreement, including liquidated damages.
low.note: With uncapped daily damages (F-01), set-off lets AtliQ hold back fees without a dispute process. Worth knowing for a vendor of this size.

low.title: Acceptance is open-ended and rests only with AtliQ
low.quote: Acceptance shall not be deemed to occur by use, by delivery to the End Client, by payment, or by the passage of time.
low.note: AtliQ has 15 days to test each deliverable, may repeat the cycle until it conforms, and acceptance never happens by silence. Combined with payment on acceptance and the delay clock running until acceptance, the vendor cannot control when it is paid or when damages stop.

low.title: Standard of performance set at 'the highest standards of the industry'
low.quote: Vendor shall perform the Services in a diligent, professional and workmanlike manner, in accordance with the highest standards of the industry, and in compliance with AtliQ's annotation guidelines and quality requirements made available to Vendor, as updated from time to time.
low.note: The guidelines can change at AtliQ's option, and the Engagement Schedule sets a 97% accuracy threshold on AtliQ-sampled QA. Worth knowing; not outside the checklist.
